# note       the transcription is Nathan D. Smith's one-token-per-line lxx-swete (from First1KGreek); Isaiah, rows 48.*, is read from First1KGreek's TEI (Swete/First1KGreek/isaiah-swete-1905.xml). Each row's why gives its evidence: a verse division the transcription lost, where Swete's own verse number stands in the text or the page prints it (and Brenton begins the verse there or near); a Latin letter for the Greek one it looks exactly like; a margin number run into a word, or a figure let into the text, taken out; two words run together, divided where Brenton's Greek and GLAUx both read them apart and Swete prints each; words the transcription lost, put back only where Brenton's Greek and GLAUx read the same words and the verse shows the hole, or where the printed page (the Internet Archive's scans of the three volumes) prints them, in the page's spelling; and verses settled one by one against the page. Misread letters are otherwise left as the transcription reads them
